documents.name: Downtown Historic District Commission Guidelines
documents.description: The Sykesville Historic District Design Guidelines provide standards for owners, tenants, architects, and contractors working within the historic district. Updated by brennan+company architects in 2023 and adopted by the Town on February 26, 2024, they cover ten topic areas: roofs, exterior walls and foundations, doors/windows/storefronts, awnings/lighting/signs, porches and decks, accessory buildings, new construction, alternate materials, sustainability/accessibility/equipment, and landscape and site design. The guidelines are administered by the Historic District Commission, which meets on the fourth Wednesday of each month.

documents.name: Historic District Commission Application
documents.description: The HDC Application packet (2023 edition) contains the application for Certificate of Approval and a sign application for projects in the Sykesville Historic District. Applications must be submitted by 4:00 PM on the second Wednesday of the month; the Commission reviews them at its fourth-Wednesday meetings. Fees: $15 residential, $25 commercial, $50 for work in progress without a permit.

documents.name: Downtown Historic District Map
documents.description: The Downtown Historic District Map, issued October 2023 by the Town of Sykesville, delineates the boundaries of the Sykesville Historic District and classifies each property as Contributing (C) or Non-Contributing (NC) based on the Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties. The accompanying property list covers approximately 160 addresses across Main Street, Springfield Avenue, Norwood Avenue, Spout Hill Road, and surrounding streets. Issued for reference purposes only; not a substitute for a survey product.

documents.name: Warfield Commercial Center New Design Guidelines
documents.description: The Warfield Commercial Center: New Construction Design Guidelines and Standards for Signs (2017 Edition) establishes design standards for new construction on the Warfield Complex, a historic former state mental hospital annexed by the Town of Sykesville. The document covers character-defining features, site plan guidelines, new building guidelines (orientation, scale, proportion, massing, materials, doors/windows, roofs), landscape guidelines, sign standards, and energy efficiency standards. Published by the Sykesville Historic District Commission in 2017 with assistance from Richard Wagner, AIA, David H. Gleason Associates, Inc.

documents.name: Warfield Commercial Center New Design Guidelines Appendix
documents.description: This appendix to the Warfield Commercial Center: New Construction Design Guidelines supplements the 2017 Edition with photographic illustrations of historic buildings in the Warfield Complex (Buildings I, W, C, D, E, Auditorium, Service Building, and others), including facade and detail photos. Its purpose is to help architects and developers understand the character-defining features of existing campus buildings that are within view corridors of proposed new construction.

documents.name: Warfield Preservation Guidelines
documents.description: The Historic Preservation Guidelines for the Warfield Complex (2002), prepared by preservation architect Richard Wagner, AIA, David H. Gleason Associates, Inc. under a federal Save America's Treasures grant, establish standards for rehabilitating the historic buildings of the former Springfield State Hospital campus. The guidelines cover exterior building materials (masonry, wood, architectural metals), roofs, windows, doors, interior spaces and structural systems, mechanical systems, energy efficiency, building additions, signs, illumination, and landscape design. Administered by the Sykesville Historic District Commission.

documents.name: HDC Minutes - November 29, 2023
documents.description: Commission approved application 2023-15 for an applied wall sign at 7524 Main Street, Suite 102 (lash bar, 14"x46" lettering, no background) - all voted in favor. Commission voted to send draft design guidelines to Town Council for approval. Brief discussion on the music shop sign at Springfield Avenue.

documents.name: Staff Report #2023-16 - 7412 Springfield Avenue
documents.description: Applicants Linda Frizzell-Makowski and David Makowski seek approval to replace roof shingles and vinyl siding on a non-contributing building (built 1994). Proposed materials: Certainteed Landmark asphalt shingles (Moire Black) and Certainteed Monogram vinyl siding 5-inch Dutch lap (Savanna Wicker), matching existing size and profile. Staff references current roof guidelines (page 26) and draft siding guidelines (page 23). No change to trim or other details.

documents.name: Application #2023-16 - 7412 Springfield Avenue
documents.description: Application materials and renderings submitted by Linda Frizzell-Makowski and David Makowski for replacement of asphalt shingles and vinyl siding on the non-contributing building at 7412 Springfield Avenue. Includes material samples for Certainteed products.

documents.name: Staff Report #2023-17 - 7568 Main Street
documents.description: Applicant Nakia Weable, new business owner; property owner Fred Gossage. Proposes two signs: (1) applied wall sign 48"x18"x1.5" thick above main door and centered above double doors on Oklahoma Avenue; (2) oval hanging business sign 30"x19"x2" thick above rear door on Oklahoma Avenue, 96" above sidewalk and 3.1 sq ft per face. Replaces existing TriSport Junction signage. Staff references current guidelines pages 36-37 and draft guidelines page 40 on applied wall signs and hanging signs.

documents.name: Application #2023-17 - 7568 Main Street
documents.description: Application materials submitted by Nakia Weable for new business signage at 7568 Main Street. Replaces TriSport Junction signage on a contributing building (built 1892). Includes diagrams of proposed applied wall sign and oval hanging sign.
